title: Arithmetic operators: + - * / % and ++ --

visuals.title: Match each operator to what it does

pairs.meaning: Division that drops the decimal part (7 / 2 is 3)
Add 1 to x first, then use it

visuals.title: If x is 5, what do you get?

goal: After this you can use + - * / % correctly, avoid the integer-division trap, and explain the difference between x++ and ++x.
warmup: A canteen splits 17 samosas between 5 students. Each student gets 3 samosas (that is division) and 2 samosas are left over (that is the remainder). Add, subtract, multiply, divide and remainder are the five basic calculations, and C++ has a symbol for each one.
definition: An operator is a symbol that does a calculation. The values it works on are called operands. In 17 + 5, the symbol + is the operator and 17 and 5 are the operands. Binary operators need two operands (+ - * / %). Unary operators need only one operand (-x, x++, ++x, x--, --x).
howItWorks: Press Play and watch the memory boxes. Binary operators calculate a new value but do not change the boxes they read from. The operators ++ and -- are special: they change the box itself by adding or subtracting 1. When ++ is written after the variable (x++) the old value is used first. When it is written before (++x) the new value is used.
syntax:
a + b      // addition
a - b      // subtraction
a * b      // multiplication
a / b      // division (int / int gives an int, decimal part is dropped)
a % b      // remainder (works only with whole numbers)
-x         // unary minus: changes the sign
x++        // postfix: use x, then add 1
++x        // prefix: add 1, then use x
x--  --x   // same idea, but subtract 1

sample.title: Five binary operators on two numbers

explanation.text: Create a box called a and store 17 in it.
Create a box called b and store 5 in it.
Multiplication uses the star symbol: 17 * 5 is 85.
Both numbers are int, so the answer is an int too. 17 divided by 5 is 3.4, but the .4 is thrown away, so we get 3.
% gives the remainder. 5 goes into 17 three times (15), and 2 is left over.

steps.note: Integer division: 17 / 5 = 3 (the decimal part .4 is dropped).
17 % 5 = 2 (the remainder). a and b never changed.

worked.problem: Show what x++ and ++x do. Start with x = 5, copy x++ into y, then copy ++x into z, and print x each time.
pseudocode: SET y = x, THEN x = x + 1
SET x = x + 1, THEN z = x
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[x = 5]
  B --> C["y = x++ : y gets 5, x becomes 6"]
  C --> D[/Print x and y/]
  D --> E["z = ++x : x becomes 7, z gets 7"]
  E --> F[/Print x and z/]
  F --> G([End])

sample.title: x++ versus ++x

explanation.text: Postfix: y takes the OLD value of x (5) first, then x goes up to 6.
Prints x = 6 and y = 5. The two are different on purpose.
Prefix: x goes up first (6 to 7), then z takes the NEW value 7.
Prints x = 7 and z = 7. Here both are the same.

steps.note: Postfix: use the old value 5 for y, THEN add 1 to x. So y = 5 and x = 6.
Print the current values of x and y.
Prefix: add 1 to x first (it becomes 7), THEN copy it into z. So z = 7.

sample.title: Convert minutes to hours and minutes

explanation.text: Integer division throws away the remainder, so this counts full hours only: 135 / 60 = 2.
% keeps only the remainder: 135 % 60 = 15 minutes left over.
Both are int, so the answer is the whole number 2.
60.0 is a decimal number, so the division is a decimal division: 2.25.

You want the remainder, or to test even/odd and divisibility
Use the old value, then add 1
variations.example: y = x++;   // x = 5 gives y = 5, x = 6

variations.when: Just add 1. On its own line both do the same thing
The result takes the sign of the left operand (checked with a real run)

mistakes.error: No error, but half becomes 0 because 1 / 2 is integer division. The compiler does not warn you.
invalid operands of types 'double' and 'int' to binary 'operator%'
lvalue required as increment operand (++ needs a variable, not a plain number)

mistakes.wrong:
int x = 5;
cout << x++;   // student expects 6
mistakes.error: No error. x++ prints the OLD value 5 and only then increases x to 6.

examTips: int / int always gives an int. 7 / 2 is 3, never 3.5.
% works only with integers. n % 2 == 0 means n is even. n % 10 gives the last digit.
x++ uses the old value; ++x uses the new value. On a line by themselves they are the same.
Do not use x++ and x (or ++x) twice in the same expression. The result is confusing and exams avoid it.
Show your working: write quotient and remainder separately, for example 17 / 5 is 3 and 17 % 5 is 2.
romanSummary: Arithmetic operators ye hain: + - * / %. % remainder deta hai, jaise 17 % 5 = 2.
Jab do int ka division hota hai to jawab bhi int aata hai, decimal hissa kat jata hai. 7 / 2 = 3.
Agar decimal chahiye to ek number decimal likho, jaise 7 / 2.0 = 3.5.
x++ pehle purani value use karta hai phir 1 barhata hai. ++x pehle 1 barhata hai phir value use karta hai.
% sirf integers ke saath chalta hai, double ke saath error aata hai.

practice.hint: Think: how much is left after taking out groups of 5?
practice.explanation: 5 fits into 17 three times (15). The leftover is 2.

practice.hint: y takes the old x. Then x goes down again before z takes it.
practice.explanation: y = x-- gives y = 8 and x = 7. Then --x makes x = 6 first, so z = 6. Final: x 6, y 8, z 6.
(a + b) is 9 and 2 is an int, so 9 / 2 is cut to 4 before it is stored. Using 2.0 makes it a decimal division: 4.5.

practice.prompt: Fill in the blank to test whether n is even: if (n ____ 2 == 0)
practice.hint: Even numbers leave no remainder when divided by 2.
practice.explanation: n % 2 is the remainder after dividing by 2. It is 0 for even numbers.

practice.hint: The remainder takes the sign of the left number, and division drops the decimal part toward zero.
practice.explanation: Checked on a real run. -7 % 3 is -1 and 7 % -3 is 1 (the sign follows the left number). -7 / 2 is -3 because the .5 is simply dropped.

practice.prompt: Write a program that stores 4825 seconds in an int and prints it as hours, minutes and seconds.
practice.hint: Use / for full units and % for what is left.
practice.explanation: 4825 / 3600 = 1 hour, 4825 % 3600 = 1225 seconds left, 1225 / 60 = 20 minutes, 4825 % 60 = 25 seconds. It prints 1 h 20 m 25 s.

quiz.prompt: What does 7 / 2 give when both are int?
quiz.explanation: int / int is integer division, so the decimal part is dropped.
The % operator returns the remainder of a division.

quiz.prompt: int x = 5; int y = x++; What are x and y?
quiz.hint: Postfix uses the old value first.
quiz.explanation: y copies 5 first, then x increases to 6.

quiz.prompt: int x = 5; int y = ++x; What are x and y?
quiz.explanation: x becomes 6 first, then y copies 6.
% works only with integers, so a double operand causes a compile error.
